title: Re-enable from 'skipped' (A6) leaves next_attempt_at NULL — row occupies its live slot but is invisible to the sweep forever
evidence:
next_attempt_at = CASE
      WHEN $2::reference_call_status IN (
        'skipped', 'partial', 'form_completed', 'unreachable', 'refused',
        'objected', 'manual_recorded', 'failed', 'completed'
      ) THEN NULL
      ELSE next_attempt_at
    END
--- contract (supabase/migrations/20260731222000_create_reference_call.sql:48): 'skipped',             -- landlord excluded this reference      [v1, A6 — re-enables to queued]
--- sweep index (same file:144): CREATE INDEX idx_reference_call_sweep
  ON reference_call(next_attempt_at) WHERE next_attempt_at IS NOT NULL;
detail: Entering 'skipped' NULLs next_attempt_at; re-enabling (skipped→queued, the A6 path) hits ELSE and preserves NULL. The partial sweep index excludes NULL rows, 'queued' still occupies the live slot, and no primitive restores the clock without appending an attempt.
recommended_fix: In update_reference_call_status, when the new status is 'queued' (re-enable), set next_attempt_at = COALESCE(next_attempt_at, now()) so a re-enabled row re-enters the sweep cadence.
